outcome: Sven Manthe (arXiv preprint, first posted 1 October 2024, revised through March 2026) proves that the monadic second-order theory of (ℝ,≤) with the set quantifier restricted to Borel sets (and even to σ-combinations of analytic sets) is decidable, confirming Saharon Shelah's 1975 conjecture on the Borel monadic theory of order (BMTO). No progress on the second half of the bullet — whether the monadic theory of well-ordering (MTWO) is consistently decidable — was found.
summary: The triage's headline finding checks out: Sven Manthe's preprint 'The Borel monadic theory of order is decidable' (arXiv:2410.00887, v1 posted 2024-10-01, v2 posted 2026-03-09) proves decidability of the monadic theory of (ℝ,≤) restricted to Borel-set quantification, resolving the first half of this bullet's two-part question (Shelah's 1975 conjecture on the BMTO). I read the paper's introduction and acknowledgements directly (via arxiv.org/html/2410.00887v1): the acknowledgements credit Philipp Hieronymi for suggesting the topic, Kim Kiehn for proofreading, and Yuri Gurevich for discussion, with no mention of any AI system, computer search, or automated tool anywhere in the paper — so ai_role is 'none'. I classify the status as 'claimed' rather than 'resolved': the paper remains an arXiv preprint by Manthe's own webpage (https://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/smanthe/), which lists it as a preprint with no journal venue, distinct from his separate, unrelated Lean-formalization paper that did appear in the Annals of Formalized Mathematics (an initial web-search summary conflated the two papers; I verified via Manthe's own publication list that the BMTO decidability paper is NOT the one published there). However there is meaningful evidence of expert engagement beyond a bare unread preprint: Manthe gave a seminar talk on the result at Oxford's Logic Seminar (14 Nov 2024, https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/69433), the result forms the core of his 2026 Bonn PhD thesis 'Decidability in Borel Monadic Logic' under advisor Philipp Hieronymi, and search results indicate he has since moved to a postdoc with Ralf Schindler at Münster — consistent with the thesis having been examined and passed by a doctoral committee, which is a form of expert vetting of the argument even without a journal referee report. A second, independent 2025/2026 preprint by Mirna Džamonja (arXiv:2512.23003, first posted 2025-12-28, v3 dated ~2026-01, using 'well-levelled orders' to code Borel sets into S2S) proves essentially the same decidability result; I could not confirm from the fetched excerpt whether it cites or disputes priority with Manthe's paper, so I am not confident this constitutes independent replication versus a second novel proof, and no priority dispute was found in what I could read. Neither paper's proof has yet been digested by a survey, blog post (I found nothing on Tao's blog or MathOverflow specifically discussing or vetting either proof), or accepted for journal publication with a referee report as far as I could establish. The MTWO consistency question (second sentence of the bullet) was not addressed by anything found — Büchi-era results establish decidability for countable ordinals and ω₁, and older Shelah-era work shows MTWO for (ω₂,<) can be made 'as complicated as you like' under different set-theoretic hypotheses (i.e. that instance is already known to be independent of ZFC), but I found no 2024–2026 work making a new claim about consistent decidability of MTWO as a whole. Given the balance — a serious, seminar-presented, thesis-anchored proof of the first half's conjecture, not yet journal-published or independently digested in print — 'claimed' is the more defensible code, with the strongest case for 'resolved' resting on the passed PhD thesis as a form of expert check (noted in competing_reading).
competing_reading: If the Bonn PhD thesis defense is treated as equivalent to 'a published verification by named experts' (a doctoral committee reading and approving the specific argument), this would meet the 'resolved' bar of an expert digestion working through the proof — the fact that Manthe has evidently completed the PhD and moved on to a postdoc is indirect but real evidence the thesis was successfully defended. I did not find a direct source confirming the defense occurred, its date, or the committee's assessment, so I coded conservatively as 'claimed'. Also worth flagging: the Džamonja preprint (2512.23003) proving apparently the same theorem independently, and whether it treats itself as confirming or as a novel/first proof (a possible unremarked priority question), is unresolved from the excerpts I could fetch.
what_would_settle_it: A confirmed date and outcome of Manthe's Bonn PhD defense; a journal acceptance notice, referee report, or an expert survey/blog digestion of arXiv:2410.00887; and a check of the Džamonja preprint's bibliography/introduction for whether it cites Manthe's priority or claims independence, which would settle whether this is one confirmed result or two.

corrections.why: F1/F2: The bullet asks two questions, BMTO decidability and MTWO consistent decidability. The record's outcome says 'No progress on the second half of the bullet … was found', so Manthe's proof settles one named part. That makes it a case, and a case is partial whatever its verification status.

events.what: Manthe proves the Borel monadic theory of (ℝ,≤) is decidable (Shelah's BMTO question)
Džamonja preprint proving decidability of MSO of the real order with Borel set quantifiers via well-levelled orders

judgement.doubts: The bullet asks two questions; only the BMTO half is addressed, and nothing on whether MTWO is consistently decidable was found. The record points to a 2026 Bonn PhD thesis containing the result, which might count as digestion (F12), but the record does not confirm the defence took place. That does not affect the code: one part of a two-part bullet is partial either way. Džamonja's later preprint is a second proof of the same case.
